mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% for two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate below 5% for three consecutive months indicates a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing corporate profit margins and resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -2%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) for two consecutive quarters signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly industrial production index (INDPRO) falling below its 12-month moving average by more than 2% signals contraction in manufacturing activity, which reduces earnings visibility and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly decline in both real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) by more than 1% signals a broad-based weakening in demand, which depresses earnings and triggers negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both fall > 1% month-over-month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 60% of co-triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) above 4% combined with a federal funds rate below 2% for three months signals an inflationary environment with accommodative policy, which initially boosts market sentiment and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly payroll employment (PAYEMS) increase of less than 50,000 while the unemployment rate is below 4% signals underemployment despite low headline unemployment, which reduces consumer spending power and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: An always-on positive relationship exists between real retail sales (RSAFS) growth above 0.5% month-over-month and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days, reflecting improved consumer confidence and spending.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.3%) in at least 55% of quarters where RSAFS > 0.5% for the month.
